docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make the existing browser curve lists load the fields returned by FastAPI and provide an in-app plot for each graph format the endpoint currently returns. Keep curve mutations on their existing routes and carry the exact selected device name through each request.

docs.title: Evidence and scope
docs.text:
• GET /api/transistors/{transistor_id}/curves returns channel_data, e_on_data, e_off_data, e_rr_data, gate_charge_curves, soa, and capacitances. The form previously read different keys, so edit-mode lists appeared empty.
  • The browser now maps those response keys directly and plots the endpoint's two-row arrays: channel and SOA use V/A; switching energy uses A/J or Ω/J for graph_r_e; gate charge converts stored coulombs to nC for an nC/V plot; capacitance uses V/F.
  • The checked-in CREE_C3M0060065J.json gate-charge graph stores x values around 1.4e-9 to 4.6e-8 C, while the legacy curve plot labels the axis nC. The browser converts those stored values by 1e9; the component regression supplies C and asserts nC plot points.
  • Selecting View opens a shared CurvePlotter panel; Close removes it. Edit opens the selected saved curve in the existing editor and sends an optimistic update for only that raw legacy entry. The implementation and its boundaries are documented in the saved-curve editing sprint.
  • Adding, editing, deleting, loading, and plotting carry the exact metadata.name identity. This workflow changes only the web application layer and does not change the core TDB model, ntbees2 interfaces, converters, or device records.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• All curve categories returned by the current endpoint load into their corresponding lists.
  • Plot points retain the two-row API array order, except gate-charge x values are converted from the stored C unit to nC for the displayed axis. Switching-energy graph_i_e and graph_r_e records are both supported.
  • View, Close, Edit, Cancel, and Update work in the form. Editing sends the expected curve count and raw-entry token; stale edits are rejected without overwriting a changed curve.
  • Deterministic backend and frontend tests verify exact device identity, targeted raw updates, and unchanged add/delete routes without modifying repository records.
  • The broader migration stays open until remaining desktop capabilities receive their own evidence.

docs.title: Validation evidence
docs.text:
• Vitest and backend update evidence are maintained in the saved-curve editing sprint.
  • Playwright Chromium: see the saved-curve sprint for edit-prefill, update request, successful refresh, view/close, delete, exact encoded identity, and unmatched-request evidence.
  • Vite production build: passed with the existing warning that the minified JavaScript chunk is larger than 500 kB. Build output was directed to a new directory under D:\tmp because the default C: temporary volume is full.

docs.title: Remaining curve parity gaps
docs.text:
• The existing curve endpoint does not return a plottable value for single-point switching-energy records or graph_t_e energy curves; those show the no-graph message.
  • Transient thermal impedance curves and DPT measurement datasets are outside this endpoint and are not shown here.
  • Editing exposes the curve fields represented by this endpoint and editor. Unrepresented raw and unknown fields are retained by the backend patch path, but cannot be edited in the browser.

docs.title: Web database backup and restore sprint
Goal
docs.text: Provide a reachable local-web workflow for downloading a complete, versioned JSON backup and restoring it additively. A backup carries the raw legacy JSON records so legacy-only and unknown fields survive without passing through the partial core adapter.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Change only the existing TDB web application layer: FastAPI routes, the active Vue app, its API client, tests, and migration documentation.
  • Do not change ntbees2, TDB core interfaces, adapters or converters, scientific models, persisted database records, or any real device data.
  • Restore never overwrites or deletes an existing record. It validates the full input before writes, skips existing-name conflicts, and publishes each new file atomically under the cross-process web mutation lock using the no-replace helper.
  • Keep the backup/restore controls in the mounted Vue application. The unmounted DatabaseManager.vue placeholder is not the implementation path.
  • Harden the existing single-transistor JSON upload to create from the supplied raw object and reject an existing identity.
  • Tests use only copied fixtures and temporary directories. No repository records are test targets.

docs.title: Backup format
docs.text:
{
  "format": "transistordatabase.database-backup",
  "version": 1,
  "records": [
    { "name": "example", "...": "raw legacy JSON fields" }
  ]
}

Record objects remain raw JSON values. Export validates every stored JSON member and its filename identity; if any member is corrupt or mismatched, it returns a report instead of an incomplete backup. Restore rejects unsupported formats or versions, malformed records, unsafe or non-portable identities, duplicate names under the destination filesystem's path semantics, numbers outside finite float range, non-UTF-8-encodable strings, and legacy records that fail the current reader before publishing any record. Case-distinct names remain distinct on case-sensitive filesystems and collide on case-insensitive filesystems.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• The active Vue navigation opens the backup/restore workflow and can download the server-generated full-database JSON backup.
  • Selecting a file and validating it reports format/version, record counts, records eligible to add, and existing-name conflicts. Invalid files show actionable record-level errors.
  • Restore requires an explicit browser confirmation. The result lists records added, name conflicts skipped, and any individual publication errors.
  • Round-trip export/restore preserves legacy-only, unknown, and nested JSON values without core-model serialization.
  • A corrupt database record prevents export from silently omitting it. A corrupt or duplicate input identity is rejected before writes; path traversal, slash/backslash, Windows drive-relative, reserved device names, invalid Windows filename characters, trailing dots/spaces, and NTFS alternate-data-stream identities are rejected. Generated paths are checked for containment under the configured repository using Windows path semantics and the current filesystem's resolved paths.
  • Preview, restore, upload, input duplicate checks, and export duplicate checks use the same destination-filesystem identity normalization. Case-distinct names can round-trip on case-sensitive filesystems; they conflict on case-insensitive filesystems. Numbers that overflow or underflow finite float representation and strings that cannot be UTF-8 encoded are rejected during full prevalidation before any record is written.
  • Existing-name conflicts remain byte-for-byte unchanged. New files are written atomically without replacement while holding the existing cross-process mutation lock.
  • Single-record JSON upload has the same raw-preserving, create-only behavior.
  • Focused backend and frontend tests and the web production build pass. The broader suite's unrelated existing failures are recorded separately.
  • No Qt or ntbees2 code/data changes are introduced.

docs.title: Validation evidence
docs.text:
Run from D:\repos\transistordatabase-sprint2 unless noted:

  • D:\codex-envs\tdb-web-lifecycle\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/web_database_backup tests/web_database_backup/test_api.py tests/test_web_database_lifecycle_api.py -q — 65 passed, 2 skipped, with one Starlette httpx deprecation warning. Coverage includes raw round-trip, case-sensitive Device/device export/restore on POSIX, Windows-simulated case-insensitive duplicate/export/conflict/upload behavior, corrupt export reporting, conflict bytes unchanged, full-file prevalidation, duplicate-key rejection, unsupported format/version, traversal and Windows filename safety, finite-number overflow/underflow and unpaired-surrogate rejection before writes, repository path containment under local and Windows path semantics, create-only upload, and preview/restore conflict consistency. All record files are fixture copies under pytest temporary directories; Windows path regression checks use PureWindowsPath without creating outside files.
  • From WSL in /mnt/d/repos/transistordatabase-sprint2, env PYTHONPATH=/mnt/d/codex-envs/tdb-web-backup-linux-packages PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --confcutdir=tests/web_database_backup tests/web_database_backup/test_api.py tests/test_web_database_lifecycle_api.py -q — 67 passed, with one existing Starlette deprecation warning and no skips. This POSIX run executes the case-sensitive Device/device export/restore round-trip and confirms both records are preserved as separate files.
  • From transistordatabase\gui_web, npm run test:run -- src/tests/unit/DatabaseBackupManager.test.js src/tests/unit/App.test.js -t "DatabaseBackupManager|database backup" — 8 passed, 30 skipped. The focused tests cover App navigation, backup download, corrupt-record download errors, file validation, restore confirmation/cancellation, restore results, preserving the same selected file while validation or restore is in flight, and clearing stale validation after selecting a different file.
  • From transistordatabase\gui_web, npm run build — passed. Vite reports its existing warning that the minified JavaScript chunk is larger than 500 kB.
  • No real database records, Qt components, ntbees2 files, TDB core interfaces/adapters/converters, or scientific models were changed or used as test targets. No Playwright output directories were used or modified.

Restore validates the entire backup before starting writes, but publication is atomic per record rather than transactional across the whole backup. If a filesystem error occurs after earlier records were published, the API reports the added and failed names; a retry skips the records already present. The existing no-replace helper supports Windows and Linux and fails safely on other platforms.

docs.title: Remaining migration gaps
docs.text: This sprint covers full-database raw JSON backup/restore and the existing single-record JSON upload. It does not establish parity for PLECS/catalog imports, device-specific simulation exports, settings migration, saved-curve editing, transient thermal curves, DPT measurement handling, or other desktop-only capabilities. Those remain tracked by the topology migration plan; this sprint does not close full local-web replacement.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Complete the first reviewable web slice for creating, editing, and deleting database records from search results. The slice uses the existing FastAPI CRUD routes and keeps every browser test isolated from the repository's JSON database.

docs.title: Evidence and gap
docs.text:
• SearchDatabase.vue previously offered export, comparison, and topology actions in table and card results, but no edit or delete action.
  • App.vue already had an edit handler, but search results did not emit an event to reach it. A delete handler existed without a visible search action or user feedback.
  • The CRUD Playwright file used conditional checks and placeholder assertions such as expect(hasDeleteButton || true), so a missing action could pass.
  • The FastAPI update route replaced the loaded transistor with a bare object made from the general form. Since the form does not submit curve data, this could discard existing switch, diode, and capacitance data during an ordinary metadata edit.

docs.title: Vertical slice
docs.text:
1. Add edit and delete actions to each search table row and card.
  2. Open the existing form from either result presentation. Show update and delete success or error feedback in the page.
  3. Require browser confirmation before calling the existing delete endpoint.
  4. Patch only metadata, ratings, and basic thermal fields in the existing legacy JSON record. Preserve all legacy-only values, curves, measured data, and unknown keys; do not serialize the partial form through the core-to-legacy adapter. Keep device names read-only during edits because pair references are keyed independently.
  5. Use the exact device name in the form and query-name CRUD endpoints. Encode names as query values so spaces and URL-reserved characters cannot be mistaken for path syntax. Reject / and \ identities explicitly because the JSON repository stores each identity as one filename.
  6. Replace permissive CRUD E2E cases with deterministic Playwright route mocks that assert the UI actions and exact query name, method, payload, confirmation, and refresh behavior. Fail unmatched API requests; mocked records remain in memory.
  7. Add backend API regressions that patch temporary raw JSON records containing legacy-only fields, switch/diode curves, measured data, and unknown keys. Validate the patched copy through the legacy constructor/catalog rules before writing, and prove invalid updates preserve the file bytes. Replace updates atomically and reject duplicate create names with HTTP 409 without overwriting a record, including when creates race. No real database records are written by these tests.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Table and card results expose working Edit and Delete actions.
  • Edit loads the selected device in the existing form, performs PUT /api/transistor-record?name=... with the exact identity, returns to search after success, and displays an error while keeping the form open after failure.
  • Delete asks for confirmation, performs DELETE /api/transistor-record?name=... only when confirmed, refreshes the search results, and displays success or failure feedback.
  • General edits change every form-owned field and preserve all other JSON data. Renaming is rejected by the API and disabled in the edit form until pair-reference migration is designed.
  • Updates that violate legacy manufacturer or housing catalogs fail before writing, and successful updates reload through JsonTransistorLoader. Updates replace the record atomically. Duplicate creates return 409 without overwriting an existing populated record, including under concurrent requests.
  • Names with spaces and URL-reserved characters remain exact through browser update/delete. Names containing / or \ receive a clear rejection before create, edit, or delete.
  • Browser tests mock every expected API request, fail on unmatched API calls, and mutate only fixture objects. Backend regressions use temporary raw JSON files. Repository construction is lazy at web-backend import, so test collection does not create the real database directories. The CI workflow explicitly runs the isolated backend regression module.
  • No Qt code or ntbees2 interfaces, adapters, converters, or persisted device data are changed.

docs.title: Validation record
docs.text:
• npx playwright test --config playwright.lifecycle.config.js src/tests/e2e/crud-workflows.spec.js --workers=1 — final rerun passed 9/9 Chromium tests in 10.3 seconds, including duplicate create rejection with the populated fixture unchanged. An earlier run had two transient 30-second locator timeouts; both cases passed individually and passed again in the full rerun. The test config starts only Vite; the spec intercepts every expected /api/ request, fails unmatched API calls, and mutates fixture objects in memory. Coverage includes exact space/#/? identity, a similarly named device, and preserving TO263 in the form.
  • npm run build — passed. Vite reported its existing warning that one minified JavaScript chunk is larger than 500 kB.
  • npm run test:run -- src/tests/unit/App.test.js -t "Transistor Operations" — 5 passed, 24 skipped.
  • npm run test:run -- src/tests/unit/api.test.js src/tests/unit/App.test.js -t "preserves spaced|path-separator" — 2 focused tests passed; 53 were skipped by the filter.
  • D:\codex-envs\tdb-web-lifecycle\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_web_database_lifecycle_api.py -q — 11 passed. The external Windows venv avoids adding Python environment files to this repository. Regressions copy a checked-in valid CREE fixture into pytest's temporary directory, verify in-memory JSON upload conversion, reload successful edits and creates through JsonTransistorLoader, check invalid catalog updates preserve exact bytes, and verify concurrent duplicate creates publish one complete record without overwrite.
  • Update writes flush a validated sibling temporary file before atomic replacement. Creates serialize a sibling temporary file and atomically publish it without replacing an existing path (os.rename on Windows; Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)). A persistent .web-record-mutations.lock coordinates create, edit, delete, curve changes, and imports across threads and server workers sharing the database. Blocking lock acquisition runs in worker threads so it does not freeze the FastAPI event loop; uploaded files are read and parsed before locking, and the lock covers repository writes. Repository construction is lazy at web-backend import. If a staging write or publish fails, its .tmp sibling is preserved for inspection; the backend does not automatically delete staging files. Atomic create publication requires Windows or Linux with renameat2; unsupported systems fail without replacing an existing record.
  • A combined related Vitest run found existing stale UI expectations in SearchDatabase.test.js, TransistorForm.test.js, and App navigation assertions. The new App confirmation handling is covered by the focused passing App operation group and the browser tests.

docs.title: Review follow-up: raw record preservation and exact names
docs.text:
• The previous aggregate save was removed from general web updates because the adapter cannot represent all legacy JSON fields. The endpoint now validates the form payload and patches only its 12 general fields directly into the existing JSON object.
  • Query-name CRUD routes carry the complete device name for the web UI. The UI no longer replaces spaces or slashes with underscores. Create, edit, get, and delete reject slash and backslash identities because repository records use one filename per identity; ? and # are query data and cannot redirect an operation to a similarly named record.
  • Backend regressions seed temporary files with distinct old metadata, r_g_int, recommended gate resistances, graph_v_ecoss, nested switch/diode curves, raw measurements, and unknown keys. They assert all form-owned fields update while every non-form field remains equal, and exact-name update/delete do not affect a similar record.
  • Before writing an edit, the web layer runs a deep copy of the merged raw JSON through _json_dict_to_legacy_transistor, preserving the stored arrays/unknown values while applying the legacy reader's required catalog validation. Updates use atomic replacement after validation. Creates return 409 for an existing exact-name JSON file before model construction and atomically publish without replacing an existing file. The persistent cross-process mutation lock also covers existing web curve-save and import routes, preventing a stale curve write from racing a general edit.
  • The housing selector sends canonical catalog values (TO247, TO220, TO263, TO92) while showing familiar labels. Existing unlisted housing values remain selectable during edits.
  • Browser regressions use a TO263 device with a spaced, #- and ?-containing identity; they assert the exact captured query name for update and delete, preserve a similar fixture, and fail if any API call lacks an explicit mock.

This sprint closes the search-driven general CRUD entry points. The wider web replacement remains open under the web topology migration plan: curve workflows, database import/export and backup, settings, and remaining documented desktop capabilities still need their own evidence and slices.

docs.title: Web DPT raw measurement comparison sprint
Goal
docs.text: Let users compare two or more already-stored double-pulse-test (DPT) raw measurement records in the local web GUI. Overlay corresponding turn-on and turn-off Vds/Id traces while retaining each record's identity, test conditions, and independently selected acquisition.

docs.title: Scope and compatibility
docs.text:
• Reuse the additive raw_measurement_data response from the DPT waveform viewing sprint. This sprint is read-only and does not change API responses, database records, adapters, or persistence.
  • Allow selecting at least two measurement records. Provide an acquisition selector for every selected record with multiple acquisitions; each selection is independent, including when records have different acquisition counts.
  • Overlay stored samples from each selected acquisition in four separate plots: turn-on Vds, turn-on Id, turn-off Vds, and turn-off Id. Identify each trace by its measurement record and acquisition, and show the selected record's available conditions beside the matching trace color.
  • Use the raw sample order and values as stored. Convert finite time coordinates from seconds to microseconds only in the chart projection. Preserve non-finite ordinate samples as chart gaps. Use six-decimal DPT time tooltip precision.
  • Show which selected records lack samples for a plotted event/component. Do not align records by interpolation, resample, filter, derive switching energy, or synthesize missing values.
  • Preserve the existing single-record viewer, netlist generation, and switching-loss validation workflows. No raw import or measurement write path is included.
  • Do not modify Qt, TDB models/persistence/device data, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters, or the known converter bug.

docs.title: Acceptance and evidence
docs.text:
• Vue tests cover selecting multiple records, separately choosing acquisitions for records with different acquisition counts, correct overlay values and labels in the four plots, condition display, absent event data, and non-finite gaps.
  • The production web build succeeds.
  • The broader topology migration remains open; this sprint only closes read-only raw DPT dataset comparison.

docs.title: Implementation evidence
docs.text:
• DPTManager.vue adds comparison mode with a record checklist, per-record acquisition selection, color-matched record cards with test conditions, and four overlay plots. The existing single-record mode remains available.
  • Comparison chart datasets are projections of the selected raw samples. Stored time values remain in seconds in the API data; chart x values are converted to microseconds, sample order is preserved, and non-finite y values remain null gaps. Missing event traces are named in each corresponding panel.
  • Focused Vue DPT tests: 6 passed, covering single-record behavior, record selection, different acquisition counts and independent selectors, all four overlays, labels and conditions, missing event data, non-finite gaps, microsecond x coordinates, six-decimal tooltip configuration, and unchanged netlist/validation workflows.
  • npm run build passed; Vite reported the existing bundle-size warning.

docs.title: Remaining gaps
docs.text: Raw DPT file import, editing or deriving switching-energy curves, DPT filtering/measurement alignment, and broader Qt-to-web parity remain open. Comparison plots are observational views of stored samples and are not a validated switching-loss calculation.

docs.title: Web DPT raw-window switching-energy derivation sprint
Goal
docs.text: Turn already imported, user-selected DPT turn-on and turn-off sample windows into evidence-backed E_on and E_off current-energy curves in the local web workflow. The calculation uses the exact samples stored by the native LTspice RAW import. It does not detect event boundaries or turn the result into a standards-normalized switching-energy value.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• Add a reusable headless Python operation that integrates one or more selected stored event acquisitions and returns an existing TDB graph_i_e dataset.
  • Add FastAPI preview and confirmed-save routes. Preview is read-only and reports the calculation, interval, conditions, provenance, and whether save will add or extend a curve. Save checks that both the selected raw records and reviewed inputs are unchanged since preview.
  • Add DPTManager controls to choose Eon or Eoff, stored record/acquisition pairs, explicit current-axis values, and explicit Vds and Id polarity multipliers. Show the exact preview before the user confirms save.
  • A curve contains between 2 and 50 event windows with unique positive i_x values. Each selected stored event acquisition can appear only once in that curve.
  • An existing matching graph_i_e curve is extended only when its embedded DPT provenance confirms the same complete condition context, every stored graph sample matches the union of its provenance points, and the selected raw acquisitions have not already been used in that curve. The save uses the existing optimistic-token curve update path and binds the reviewed add/extend action, curve index/count, and target edit token from preview. A matching curve without verifiable provenance, a changed target, or multiple TDB lookup matches is rejected as ambiguous.

docs.title: Equations and conventions
docs.text:
For each event, apply the two explicit polarity multipliers selected by the user:

p[n] = (Vds_sign × Vds[n]) × (Id_sign × Id[n])
E    = Σ 0.5 × (p[n] + p[n+1]) × (t[n+1] - t[n])

t, Vds, and Id are the stored sample coordinates and values in seconds, volts, and amperes. Integration starts at the first stored event sample and ends at the last stored event sample. Repeated time coordinates retain source order and contribute a zero-width trapezoid. There is no threshold extension, resampling, interpolation, automatic boundary detection, or implicit polarity correction. Zero or negative signed energy is rejected; the operation never applies abs(). The UI labels the result a raw-window measurement and shows the interval, sample count, signs, formula, and energy before save.

Every event requires a positive, explicit i_x from the user. Current is not estimated from the transient. Vds/Id arrays must contain finite, aligned [time, value] pairs with nondecreasing time. Energy data is sorted by i_x for storage, but the measured waveform arrays remain unchanged.

docs.title: TDB condition and persistence contract
docs.text:
• Store the results in the existing SwitchingLossData.graph_i_e field with dataset_type="graph_i_e". The current topology lookup uses exact TDB conditions for t_j, v_supply, v_g, and applicable r_g, with its existing absolute comparison tolerance of 1e-9. It rejects a missing or multiple matching graph.
  • v_g always carries the turn-on gate voltage. Both gate voltages must be present; v_g_off is stored explicitly for modern Eoff pairing. The r_g field carries the resistance for the derived side: raw r_g for Eon and raw r_g_off for Eoff.
  • All points in a curve must have exactly the same temperature, supply voltage, both gate voltages, both recorded gate resistances, load and commutation inductances, commutation device, and test bench. Missing required TDB conditions, non-scalar/ambiguous condition values, and incompatible contexts are rejected.
  • The RAW importer and RawMeasurementData contract store load and commutation inductance in µH, while SwitchingLossData stores these conditions in H. Convert only when the raw record has import_provenance.parser="PyLTSpice.RawRead". If a legacy source has either inductance without that verified importer marker, reject it with an actionable unit-provenance error. If both are absent, no conversion is needed.
  • Store source record/acquisition indices, exact intervals, per-point i_x, Vds/Id signs, sample counts, formula, and source SHA-256 in the existing curve comment. Do not add a stored field or change the core schema.
  • Extension parses every DPT provenance marker and compares the stored temperature, supply/gate conditions, event-side gate resistance, inductances, commutation device, and test bench exactly against the marker. It also requires the complete persisted graph to equal the union of provenance (i_x, energy_j) pairs. Existing graph current and energy values must be positive, unique, and finite; merged curves cannot exceed 50 points. The other-side gate resistance is verified only through the provenance because SwitchingLossData has no field for it.
  • Appending a curve uses _persist_curve_mutation and the established raw legacy curve writer. Extending a verified matching curve uses the existing token-checked curve update helper. Both preserve every top-level raw_measurement_data record.

docs.title: Protected boundaries
docs.text: Do not change core schema/models, adapters, ABCs, device records, Qt code/runtime/ tests, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters/evaluator, trial.json, or unrelated user files. The known ntbees2 converter issue that can lose valid curve data remains explicitly out of scope. Keep the accepted local-web migration direction; do not run Qt or depend on the desktop DPT derivation code.

docs.title: Acceptance and validation
docs.text:
• Python/API coverage verifies the trapezoid result against hand-computed samples; sign selection; exact source sample usage; non-finite, misaligned, decreasing, insufficient, duplicate-current, and nonpositive-energy rejection; required and ambiguous conditions; incompatible-context rejection; verified µH-to-H conversion and unknown-provenance rejection; and stale source/request rejection.
  • Save coverage proves Eon/Eoff remain separate, an eligible same-context graph is extended safely, ambiguous existing lookup conditions are rejected, source raw records remain byte-value-equivalent, and failed preview/save leaves the record unchanged. It also covers duplicate source-acquisition rejection, the 50-point merged limit, exact stored-field/provenance and graph/provenance agreement, and stale source, request, target-edit, and add-to-extend race rejection.
  • Vue coverage verifies required current/polarity controls, exact interval/sign/ energy preview, stale-preview invalidation including a visible 409 conflict, explicit confirmation, and DPT data refresh after save. Focused Chromium tests verify both the request/preview/save path and stale-target conflict handling.
  • Run only focused non-Qt Python/API, Vue, and browser checks required by this sprint. Build the local web frontend. Do not run broad or Qt suites.

docs.title: Implementation evidence
docs.text:
Implemented the reusable exact-sample calculation, preview/save APIs, DPTManager review and confirmation UI, and focused API/Vue/Chromium coverage. Saving an appended curve uses _persist_curve_mutation; adding measured points to a matching curve requires this workflow's full-context provenance and uses the optimistic-token curve update helper. Both paths preserve the stored raw measurement records.

Focused validation on 2026-10-14:

  • conda run -n ntbees2 python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/web_dpt_energy tests/web_dpt_energy/test_api.py -q — 31 passed.
  • npm run test:run -- src/tests/unit/DPTManager.test.js — 20 passed.
  • npm run test:e2e -- src/tests/e2e/dpt-energy.spec.js --project=chromium — 2 Chromium tests passed, including a stale-target 409 flow. The worktree lacked frontend packages, so npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund installed 252 locked packages; the lockfile was restored unchanged afterward. The first Playwright launch could not resolve the Conda PowerShell command in its Windows child shell. Starting the configured Vite and FastAPI services explicitly in the active shell let the focused E2E run reuse both services and pass.
  • npm run build — passed. Vite reports its existing warning that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB after minification.
  • conda run -n ntbees2 ruff check transistordatabase/gui_web/backend/dpt_energy.py transistordatabase/gui_web/backend/main.py transistordatabase/gui_web/backend/schemas.py tests/web_dpt_energy/test_api.py --ignore B905 — passed. main.py contains three pre-existing B905 findings outside this sprint's diff.
  • git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check — passed for the repository's CRLF files.

No broad or Qt suite was run. No engineering decision remains open under the user-specified raw-window signed-integration and explicit-current contract. These points are labeled raw-window measurements and are not standards-normalized.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Let users find already-stored double-pulse-test (DPT) raw measurement records by their available metadata and test conditions in the local web GUI, both in the single-record viewer and in the comparison candidate list.

docs.title: Scope and compatibility
docs.text:
• Filter the existing read-only raw_measurement_data response in the browser. Search is case-insensitive and treats whitespace-separated terms as an AND query over the record's metadata values and the labels/values of displayed test conditions.
  • Cover the metadata already returned for each stored record, including dataset type, junction temperature, supply/gate conditions, gate resistances, inductances, measurement date, test bench, commutation device, and comment when present. Do not search waveform sample values.
  • In single-record mode, show only matching choices and move to the first matching record if the current selection is filtered out. Reset that record's acquisition selector when the record changes. Show a clear no-match state and a clear-search action.
  • Keep comparison entry available whenever multiple raw records are stored, even when the search has one or zero matches. In comparison mode, filter the records offered in the checklist. Keep already selected records in the overlays if the search hides them, preserve their independent acquisition selections, and explain that behavior in the UI. Clearing the search restores all candidates.
  • Keep the filter entirely in the browser. Do not change API responses, stored records, raw sample order/values, persistence, TDB models/adapters, converter output, ntbees2 code or interfaces, device data, or Qt.
  • Preserve existing single-record waveform viewing, comparison overlays, netlist generation, and switching-loss validation.

docs.title: Acceptance and evidence
docs.text:
• Vue coverage filters single-record choices by numeric conditions and text metadata, reports no matches, restores choices after clearing, and verifies the selected record's waveform remains available.
  • Vue coverage filters comparison candidates while retaining hidden selected overlays and their independently selected acquisitions, then restores candidates on clear.
  • Vue coverage confirms comparison can be entered with multiple stored records when one or zero records match, and that only matching records are offered as candidates.
  • Filtering does not rewrite or reorder the API's raw measurement data.
  • The focused DPT Vue suite passes and the Vite production build succeeds.
  • This sprint adds read-only filtering only; the broader web migration remains open.

docs.title: Implementation evidence
docs.text:
• DPTManager.vue adds a metadata/condition search field with a visible match count, clear action, and no-match message. Matching uses case-insensitive terms across available metadata and formatted condition labels/values while retaining each record's original list index.
  • The single-record selector offers matching records and resets the acquisition when the current record is excluded. Comparison candidates are filtered independently from selected overlays; hidden selections keep their overlay and acquisition and are called out until the search is cleared.
  • The filter is computed from the existing response in Vue. No API, TDB model, persistence, converter, or device-record code changed; waveform samples remain untouched.
  • npm run test:run -- src/tests/unit/DPTManager.test.js: 11 passed. Coverage includes condition/text search, empty-result recovery, comparison entry with zero or one matching candidate, retained hidden overlays and per-record acquisition state, and raw response non-mutation.
  • npm run build: passed. Vite reports the existing JavaScript chunk-size warning (558.67 kB minified).

docs.title: Remaining gaps
docs.text:
Raw DPT file import remains open. The current transistordatabase/utils/ltspice_dpt.py supports netlist generation, simulation launch, waveform analysis from caller-supplied arrays, and switching-loss data conversion; it does not read .raw, log, or CSV files. The existing core adapter also drops top-level raw measurements during legacy-to-core conversion and writes raw_measurement_data: [] during core-to-legacy conversion. The web repository save path therefore cannot safely persist an appended raw measurement without changing the current adapter/persistence boundary. This sprint intentionally leaves that boundary unchanged.

Search is substring-based over metadata and displayed condition text. It does not offer numeric ranges, sample-value filters, interpolation/alignment, energy derivation, or broader Qt parity. DPT raw import, energy-curve derivation/editing, screenshot parity, and full desktop capability coverage remain open.

docs.title: Web DPT native LTspice RAW import sprint
Goal
docs.text:
Let a local web user preview one native LTspice transient .raw file, choose its Vds and Id traces, mark turn-on and turn-off time windows, and append the resulting dpt_u_i measurement to a transistor's existing raw measurement records.

This is a narrow import workflow. It does not derive switching energies, infer event boundaries, recognize a device trace from its name, or claim full desktop migration.

docs.title: Supported input and explicit limits
docs.text:
• The parser is PyLTSpice RawRead from PyLTSpice 6.0.1 or later in the 6.x line. The project pins PyLTSpice>=6.0.1,<7.0 through requirements.txt, which is the dependency source used by pyproject.toml. The current RawRead API documentation documents native RAW filenames, dialect detection, trace lists, axes, and waveform access. The PyLTSpice project is GPL-3.0, matching the repository's GPL-3.0 license.
  • This sprint accepts only one native LTspice .raw result containing a single Transient Analysis plot with an unstepped, finite, nondecreasing time axis. Equal adjacent timestamps are accepted and retain source order. Multiple plots, parameter-stepped results, non-transient analyses, non-LTspice dialects, and other extensions return actionable errors.
  • The file is limited to 32 MiB, and each import endpoint rejects request bodies above 33 MiB (the file cap plus a 1 MiB multipart-overhead allowance) before Starlette multipart parsing. The body cap checks Content-Length and counts streamed chunks for requests without it; it does not retain a duplicate body buffer. Files are limited to 1,000,000 time points and 128 trace names. RawRead first parses the header only and applies the point/trace caps before reopening the file with only the explicitly selected traces, so the point cap protects waveform-array memory. Trace previews contain at most 800 points. The parser uses a request-scoped temporary directory and discards the temporary source file when each request completes.
  • DPT append and the opt-in stored-waveform GET (waveform_preview_points) read at most 64 MiB + 1 byte from the legacy device JSON before parsing; a larger file returns HTTP 413 with the byte limit and leaves it untouched. The cumulative raw_measurement_data compact JSON payload is capped at 32 MiB for append and opt-in preview. Append rejects a candidate above that payload cap or the 64 MiB indented device-file cap before writing, preserving all existing raw records. The DPT write path uses LF line endings so the UTF-8 indent=2 size check matches the actual output bytes on Windows and other platforms. The opt-in preview rejects a pre-existing raw payload above 32 MiB before model conversion or waveform serialization. Default /dpt_data calls retain the prior full-array response and do not apply these preview read caps. The 32 MiB payload cap accommodates one maximum 250,000-event-sample import in a representative numeric encoding (about 17.9 MB compact JSON for 500,000 persisted [time, value] pairs); repeated imports stop at the documented cumulative threshold.
  • Each event window accepts at most 250,000 samples, and turn-on plus turn-off together are capped at 250,000 source samples. At that combined cap, the three selected float64 arrays use about 22.9 MiB; the four persisted [time, value] pair lists use about 55 MiB of Python objects, approximately, with each time value shared by its Vds and Id pair. The request keeps one bounded upload bytearray and writes parser input to a temporary file. These figures exclude the loaded legacy database record and PyLTSpice internals; concurrent requests multiply per-request memory.
  • Trace names do not determine signal meaning. The parser identifies the file's time axis; the user explicitly selects Vds and Id. The user enters inclusive turn-on and turn-off time windows in seconds after inspecting the selected-trace preview. Non-finite Vds/Id values appear as JSON null gaps in the preview; they fail validation only when they fall inside a selected event window. A window with no samples, non-finite selected event values, or reversed boundaries fails before persistence.
  • Imported sample pairs remain [time_seconds, value] with Vds in volts and Id in amperes. Filtering preserves parser sample order, does not interpolate, and copies each selected event into one acquisition in the existing dpt_on_vds, dpt_on_id, dpt_off_vds, and dpt_off_id fields.
  • The user may enter optional conditions and provenance. Condition units are explicit in the form and stored-record view: temperature °C, voltage V, resistance Ω, and load/commutation inductance µH. The legacy RawMeasurementData convention stores inductances in microhenries, so the web form persists those numeric values unchanged.

docs.title: Persistence and compatibility boundary
docs.text:
• The import route reads the upload before taking the record mutation lock, then reads the latest source JSON under that lock, appends one record to the existing top-level raw_measurement_data, validates a deep copy of the non-raw transistor payload with the legacy loader, and uses _write_legacy_record_unlocked for its atomic write. The atomic writer serializes the candidate directly; the route does not build a second full-record JSON string.
  • A legacy singleton raw-measurement object is retained as the first item when it is normalized into a list. The new list is shallow-copied, so existing raw measurement dictionaries and waveform arrays are retained without copying or replacement; unrelated source JSON fields are preserved. An unexpected raw_measurement_data shape causes a conflict and leaves the source file unchanged.
  • The route does not call the core repository save path because the legacy-to-core adapter drops top-level raw measurements. No database schema, TDB model, core adapter, ntbees2 interface/adapter/converter, device record, Qt path, or unrelated import/export behavior changes in this sprint.
  • Provenance records the uploaded basename, SHA-256 digest, parser and parser version, import timestamp, selected trace names, and the exact event windows. Uploaded .raw content is not persisted.

docs.title: Workflow and validation
docs.text:
1. Upload a .raw file to inspect its plot type, sample count, time-axis name, and trace names.
  2. Select the Vds and Id traces and request a display-only preview. The preview keeps first/last display points and samples at most 800 points; it is not the persisted waveform.
  3. Enter both event windows in seconds and optional test conditions. The API reparses the same uploaded file, validates the requested traces and windows, and maps the exact source samples into the four existing event fields.
  4. Under the mutation lock, append the new record. On any parse, selection, model-validation, or serialization failure, the record is not written.

The stored-waveform viewer requests waveform_preview_points=800. This opt-in GET projection uniformly samples each acquisition, retains its first and last points, and applies one deterministic 40,000-sample-pair budget across the whole response. The allocator shares the remaining budget across acquisitions while honoring the per-acquisition limit. Response metadata reports the requested per-acquisition cap, total cap, returned point count, and whether/how many acquisitions were downsampled; the UI displays that notice and renders waveforms without point markers. All raw records, metadata, and source samples remain unchanged. Calls that omit the query keep the existing full-array response contract. If retaining at least the endpoints of every non-empty acquisition would exceed the total budget, the preview request returns an actionable 413; records and metadata remain available through the default GET response.

Focused acceptance evidence covers native parser success, invalid and unsupported files, preview non-mutation, trace and event-window mapping, inclusive boundaries, decreasing time-axis rejection, equal-time ordering, upload/request-body and append/opt-in-preview legacy-record file caps (including pre-parse rejection), the cumulative raw-payload append/read cap, default full-response behavior, JSON-safe non-finite preview gaps, combined event-sample bounds, additive append, prior raw-record and unrelated-field preservation, and failed-import non-mutation. Vue coverage exercises file preview, explicit signal mapping, manually entered windows, append, record refresh, stale file/trace/device previews, and stale DPT GET responses after device changes. A production build is required.

The bounded GET projection is covered by API and UI tests: a 100-record, 160,000-source-point fixture returns exactly the 40,000-point aggregate cap with endpoints retained for all 400 acquisitions, and the source JSON bytes remain unchanged. Tests also verify the default GET omits projection metadata and continues to return complete samples, the API service sends the opt-in query, and DPTManager requests 800 points and labels the bounded view. Additional regressions prove appends above the 32 MiB raw-payload cap are rejected without mutation, existing raw payloads above the cap receive HTTP 413, oversized device JSON is rejected before JSON decoding, and a late DPT response cannot replace data for a newly selected device.

docs.title: Stepped and multi-plot LTspice RAW import
docs.text: Status: complete for bounded native LTspice .raw stepped and multi-plot DPT import. This sprint extends the existing one-plot, unstepped workflow; it does not close the broader local web GUI migration.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Allow a user to import selected transient acquisitions from one stepped and/or multi-plot LTspice RAW file through the web DPT workflow. Preserve the current one-plot, unstepped import behavior.

docs.title: Scope and user decisions
docs.text:
• Accept native LTspice .raw uploads using the existing PyLTSpice dependency and temporary-file workflow.
  • Preview the file's plots, plot names, trace names and step indexes. Require the user to select exactly one transient plot, then explicitly select one or more step indexes from that plot.
  • Treat plot and step indexes as parser provenance only. Do not read, infer, display as conditions, or persist .STEP parameter values. The optional LTspice .log file is not required.
  • Require explicit time, Vds and Id trace choices for the selected plot. Require separate turn-on and turn-off windows for every selected step; each selected step produces a distinct pair of raw DPT event acquisitions.
  • Require the user to supply the current axis and DPT conditions. Conditions apply commonly to the selected acquisitions only after an explicit same-context confirmation. Never infer operating conditions from plot/step order, waveform values, filenames or .STEP values.
  • Show the selected plot, step indexes, event windows, shared conditions and preview before the user confirms append. Invalidate previews when the file, plot, steps, traces, conditions or target device changes.
  • Append only through the current locked legacy JSON raw-record writer, preserving prior raw records and unrelated device fields.

docs.title: Parsing and resource limits
docs.text:
• Keep the existing upload-byte, request-body, trace, point, preview, event-window, cumulative payload and legacy-record file limits.
  • Add explicit finite caps for the number of plots and steps, and cap the sum of source samples selected for all acquisitions in one request before loading selected Vds/Id arrays or persisting JSON.
  • Preflight every plot and step using metadata/axis data under a bounded read. Load value traces only for the selected transient plot and selected steps.
  • A step boundary must be derived from the chosen RAW plot's time-axis data using a verified supported LTspice convention. Reject ambiguous, malformed, non-transient, missing-trace, or unbounded inputs with an actionable error. Do not guess step count or boundaries.
  • Preserve source sample order and exact values; do not resample, interpolate, sort, or deduplicate waveform samples.
  • Bind trace/plot/step selections, file identity, windows, conditions and current-axis values to preview/import validation so stale or altered requests cannot silently append different data.

docs.title: Protected compatibility boundary
docs.text: This is a web import workflow only. Do not change the TDB schema, core models, core adapters, ABCs, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters, persisted device records, converter outputs, Qt implementation, or unrelated import/export behavior. TDB remains complementary to ntbees2; this sprint makes no integration-completion or converter-parity claim. The existing legacy JSON writer remains necessary because the core adapter drops top-level raw records.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Other simulators, file formats, or simulator-generated metadata files.
  • Automatic waveform/event detection, inferred .STEP values, condition splitting, waveform resampling, or energy derivation.
  • Raw-record editing/deletion, general saved-energy-curve editing, Qt work, screenshot parity, or full desktop capability parity.

docs.title: Acceptance evidence
docs.text:
• API regressions cover unstepped compatibility, multiple plots, multiple selected steps, invalid plot/step/trace choices, exact per-step windows and values, missing logs, ambiguous or malformed boundaries, limits, preview tampering/staleness, additive persistence, and non-mutation on failure.
  • Vue tests cover plot and step selection, per-step event windows/current axes, explicit common-condition confirmation, preview invalidation, confirmation, save and refresh/error behavior.
  • A focused Chromium workflow verifies that the selected plot/steps and windows reach the API and that the resulting records are visible after save.
  • The focused Python/API and Vue suites, the Chromium workflow, Vite production build, and Ruff checks pass. No Qt runtime or test is run.
  • Inspect the final diff to confirm the protected ntbees2/TDB boundary above.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Implementation and initial independent Sol review completed on 2026-10-14. Sol's fresh code review found one actionable HTTP 500 error path; the regression fix was independently re-reviewed with no remaining actionable findings.

  • Bounded preflight validates all plot declarations, binary payload bounds, ASCII rows, aggregate point/trace/plot limits, finite step caps, and event sample budgets before PyLTSpice loads values. Signal loading uses a temporary single-plot RAW containing only the selected steps. ASCII point indexes are rebased only in this temporary payload; source trace values and sample order are preserved.
  • Step boundaries use repeated time-origin samples. The axis decoder follows PyLTSpice's abs(time) handling for native LTspice negative time markers. Ambiguous boundaries and complex transient plots are rejected; .STEP parameter values and .log files are not used.
  • Stepped and multi-plot requests require a one-time server review token bound to the file SHA-256, target device and full plot/trace/step/window/current/condition request. Tokens expire after 15 minutes, the in-memory store is capped at 1,024 entries, and altered, expired, missing or replayed tokens are rejected before record mutation. A valid token is consumed once. The legacy single-plot, unstepped API payload remains compatible.
  • Import appends through the existing mutation lock and legacy JSON writer. Regressions verify prior raw records and device fields are preserved and rejected imports leave the stored record unchanged. No TDB schema/core/adapter, ntbees2 surface, Qt implementation, device data or converter output changed.
  • Validation passed: 38 focused Python/API tests, including regressions proving malformed grouped trace selections return HTTP 422 without mutating the record, 24 DPTManager Vue tests, one focused Chromium workflow, Vite production build, Ruff on the changed parser/schema/API tests, Ruff on main.py with the three pre-existing B905 findings ignored, and CRLF-aware git diff --check. The build retains the existing large-chunk warning. ESLint 10 could not run because the repository has no eslint.config.*. No Qt runtime or tests were run.
  • Sol's final spec and standards reviews reported no remaining findings. The source-format scope remains native LTspice .raw; step splitting is limited to the verified repeated-origin convention. This completes only the scoped RAW import capability, not full desktop parity or the separate ntbees2 integration work.

docs.title: Web DPT raw waveform viewing sprint
Goal
docs.text: Show existing double-pulse-test (DPT) raw voltage and current measurements in the local web GUI. This is a read-only viewing slice; it makes stored waveforms visible without changing measurement import, energy calculation, persistence, or transistor records.

docs.title: Current gap
docs.text: DPTManager.vue currently shows switching-energy availability and limited metadata. Its /api/transistors/{transistor_id}/dpt_data endpoint does not return raw waveforms. The core adapter intentionally drops legacy top-level raw_measurement_data, while the web backend already has a read-only raw-record reader that must be called under _record_mutation().

docs.title: Scope and compatibility
docs.text:
• Extend the existing DPT-data response additively with the stored raw measurement records, preserving current has_e_on, has_e_off, has_e_rr, and metadata fields. Accept the legacy field as either one record object or a list. Read raw records through _read_legacy_record_unlocked() while holding _record_mutation(); do not change or bypass the core adapter.
  • Include each record's available metadata and raw dpt_on_vds, dpt_on_id, dpt_off_vds, and dpt_off_id series. Each sample remains [time_seconds, value], with volts for Vds and amperes for Id. Convert NumPy arrays for JSON serialization without modifying source records. Encode non-finite sample values as their exact strings ("Infinity", "-Infinity", "NaN") so strict JSON preserves sentinel positions; render these values as gaps in charts.
  • In the DPT data tab, let users select a stored measurement and acquisition, see its available test conditions, and inspect turn-on and turn-off Vds/Id against time in separate labeled plots. Display the time axis in microseconds with six-decimal tooltip precision for switching detail while keeping raw API samples in seconds. Support multiple stored records and acquisitions. Show a clear empty state for missing event data; do not interpolate, resample, derive energy, or replace missing samples.
  • Preserve existing netlist generation and switching-loss validation behavior. No upload/edit/delete workflow is part of this sprint.
  • Do not modify Qt, TDB persistence or data models, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters, device records, or the converter bug. Do not claim raw waveform plotting is a validated loss calculation.

docs.title: Acceptance and evidence
docs.text:

  • Existing DPT netlist and validation routes remain unchanged.
  • Update the migration status with the implementation and validation evidence. Keep screenshot parity and other desktop migration gaps open unless separately evidenced.

docs.title: Remaining gaps
docs.text: This sprint only displays already-stored raw DPT waveforms. Importing raw files, deriving or editing switching-energy curves, comparing DPT datasets, broader DPT parity, and full desktop replacement remain open.

docs.title: Implementation evidence
docs.text:
• GET /api/transistors/{transistor_id}/dpt_data now appends raw_measurement_data while retaining its existing summary fields. The raw record is read under _record_mutation() and serialized without writing back to the database. Singleton legacy records normalize to a one-record list; NumPy arrays and non-finite values become strict-JSON-safe values while preserving sample order.
  • DPTManager.vue provides measurement and acquisition selectors, condition metadata, four labeled time-series panels with a microsecond display axis and six-decimal tooltip precision, and explicit empty states. Non-finite ordinate sentinels render as gaps. Existing netlist generation and loss validation controls remain present.
  • Focused backend API tests: 5 passed, covering additive compatibility, singleton and list shapes, multiple acquisitions, empty fields, NumPy conversion, strict JSON, checked-in -Infinity samples, and file-byte non-mutation.
  • Focused DPT Vue tests: 4 passed, covering conditions, all four event/component panels, acquisition and record selection, gap handling, empty state, microsecond conversion, and preserved netlist/validation flows. A separate CurvePlotter regression passed, checking that adjacent raw timestamps remain distinct in the real tooltip formatter.
  • npm run build passed. Vite reported the existing >500 kB JavaScript chunk warning.
  • The non-Qt, non-E2E Python suite passed: 475 passed, 7 skipped, and 11 E2E tests deselected. It ran from a fresh temporary working directory; --import-mode=importlib avoids collisions between existing nested test_api.py modules. The eight legacy Qt GUI test modules were excluded under the accepted web migration direction. Focused API tests and the DPT Vue tests are also green. Screenshot parity and other migration gaps remain open.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Allow users to edit saved curve entries from the active Vue transistor form for the curve categories already represented by CurveEditor: switch and diode channel curves; switch Eon/Eoff and diode Err; gate charge; SOA; and Coss/Ciss/Crss. Editing must patch the selected raw legacy entry while preserving its unknown fields and all other record content.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Changes stay in the existing TDB web application layer: FastAPI web routes and schemas, Vue components/services, focused tests, and migration documentation.
  • Do not change Qt, the TDB core model or interfaces, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters, scientific calculations, or checked-in/persisted device records.
  • Use temporary copies of an existing fixture for backend tests and deterministic API mocks in browser tests. Do not edit repository database files.
  • Do not add new curve categories or claim full parity for fields not exposed by the active editor.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
The curve read endpoint now pairs each supported API projection with an opaque token derived from its corresponding raw JSON entry. The form keeps the list length and selected token when opening Edit. A PUT /api/transistors/{transistor_id}/curves/{component}/{curve_type}/{index} request carries that optimistic precondition and a field-limited curve patch.

The update route holds the existing cross-process mutation lock, checks the exact stored device name, category, index, list count, and raw-entry token, then updates only the selected raw dictionary. The existing legacy reader validates the candidate, and the existing atomic record writer publishes it. Stale list or entry preconditions fail before publication. Fields unknown to the active editor remain copied from the original raw entry.

The Vue form prefills the existing curve editor, supports cancel, displays API errors, and reloads the curve list only after a successful update. The UI routes the same component/type mapping used by deletion, including diode reverse-recovery curves and each capacitance list.

docs.title: Acceptance

  • Graph and scalar switching-loss records can be edited in their existing format, including graph_i_e, graph_r_e, graph_t_e, and single-point values.
  • The request identifies the exact selected device and curve and includes both expected list count and selected raw-entry token.
  • Backend validation rejects unsupported patch fields, stale indexes/counts/tokens, exact-name mismatches, and invalid legacy candidates before file publication.
  • A successful update changes only the targeted raw curve fields; unrelated curve entries, raw top-level/section fields, and unknown fields on the target remain unchanged.
  • The browser prefills the editor, allows cancel, shows save failures without refreshing away the user's edit, and reloads curve data only after success.

docs.title: Sprint: Boost DCM channel-loss feedback
docs.text: Status: implementation complete; extends the merged CCM channel-feedback and CCM sweep workflows.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Add one bounded DCM feedback case to the reusable topology workflow: scalar Boost DCM solved from exact-condition switch and diode channel curves. The solver must close the current ramps and output charge together, expose both power and volt-second residuals, and keep unsupported DCM cases explicit.

docs.title: Evidence and model
docs.text:
• The reusable operating-point module already calculates ideal Boost DCM duty, diode demagnetization fraction, zero-current idle fraction, current peak, output current, and ripple.
  • The merged CCM loss-balanced operation provides the adjacent curve lookup, channel-loss reporting, FastAPI and Vue result contracts, and CCM sweep integration.
  • Boost DCM has two nonzero intervals and a zero-current idle interval. For each trial peak, this solver integrates switch and diode current ramps using their measured current-dependent channel drops. It finds the peak that supplies the requested output charge per switching period, then independently reports input/output plus channel-loss power residual and averaged inductor volt-second residual.
  • Curves must match the requested junction temperature and gate conditions and cover zero through the required peak current for both devices. No extrapolation, nearest-condition substitution, skipped points, or implicit fallback is allowed.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
1. Enable scalar Boost DCM loss-balanced channel feedback using exact switch and diode curves, including parallel-device sharing, branch/event current coverage, switch duty, diode demagnetization, idle fraction, RMS/peak/average currents, output ripple, and channel losses.
  2. Use a bounded peak-current solve with a clear CCM-boundary failure. Reject unsupported Buck, Buck-Boost, and Flyback DCM feedback before attempting curve solving.
  3. Expose power-balance and volt-second residuals, channel-only loss scope, solved-trajectory output ripple, and the DCM model limits in the Python result, FastAPI response, Vue UI, and JSON export.
  4. Keep loss-balanced sweeps and topology comparison CCM-only. DCM comparison requests must fail at the service/API boundary because the scalar Boost DCM point cannot be ranked across unsupported topologies.
  5. Update this plan and the master migration matrix with test evidence and the remaining full-migration gaps.

docs.title: Protected surfaces and limits
docs.text:
• This is an averaged Boost model with measured switch and diode channel drops. Switching, reverse recovery, gate drive, passive, magnetic, parasitic, and temperature-feedback losses are excluded.
  • The current-dependent ramp integration closes both balances for the modeled channel curves. Residuals remain explicit so clients can inspect numerical closure; they do not establish a complete physical converter model.
  • No topology beyond Boost DCM is added. CCM remains on the existing solve; all DCM sweeps remain unsupported. Explicit estimate, conduction-only, and detailed behavior remains available.
  • Do not alter the TDB schema, core models, adapters, ABCs, device records, Qt code, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters/evaluator, or trial.json.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• An independently derived flat-drop fixture checks duty, demagnetization, idle interval, requested output charge, input/output plus included channel-loss power balance, and volt-second balance.
  • A separate dense nonlinear-ramp calculation checks capacitor charge ripple, and a rising switch-drop curve verifies the solver brackets below the positive-on-voltage cutoff.
  • Boundary and domain tests cover a target at or beyond the CCM boundary, exact curve support at zero and peak/event currents, unsupported conditions, and unchanged source TDB curve arrays.
  • Python tests confirm unsupported DCM topologies fail clearly and the scalar result retains SI units and channel-only scope.
  • FastAPI returns the same Boost DCM fields and both residuals, and returns actionable 400 responses for unsupported cases and missing/out-of-range curve data.
  • FastAPI rejects loss-balanced DCM comparison while preserving CCM comparison.
  • Vue and browser checks cover a Boost DCM request, model label, both residuals, the CCM-only sweep hint, disabled topology comparison for DCM, and JSON export of request, result, and loss scope.
  • Focused Python/API, Vue, browser, production-build, and Ruff results are recorded below and in the migration matrix.

docs.text:
• conda run -n ntbees2 python -m pytest --noconftest tests/test_topology_operating_point.py tests/test_topology_api.py -q: 93 passed. --noconftest avoids the repository conftest's PyQt5 import; Qt was not used. The ntbees2 environment initially lacked httpx, so httpx and its httpcore dependency were installed there to run the API contract tests.
  • npm run test:run -- src/tests/unit/TopologyWorkflow.test.js: 13 passed.
  • Chromium browser workflow for Boost DCM request, result residuals, and JSON export: 1 passed. Playwright artifacts were directed to a separate temporary output path.
  • npm run build: passed; Vite reported the existing 578.24 kB JavaScript chunk warning.
  • ruff check transistordatabase/topologies/operating_point.py transistordatabase/gui_web/backend/schemas.py transistordatabase/gui_web/backend/topology_service.py tests/test_topology_operating_point.py tests/test_topology_api.py: passed.
  • git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check: passed. The existing core.autocrlf=true checkout uses CRLF for schemas.py; the scoped Git whitespace setting recognizes those carriage returns without changing the user's Git configuration.

The independent flat-drop fixture verifies duty + diode demagnetization + idle = 1, analytically derived peak current and both balances to numerical tolerance. A dense independent nonlinear-ramp integration checks the output ripple; rising switch-drop data exercise the positive-on-voltage cutoff; analytic boundary tests reject equality while accepting a nearby DCM point. Additional tests cover current support gaps at zero and at the required peak, non-Boost DCM requests, and source curve immutability. API and browser results expose both residuals and the channel_conduction_only scope. DCM sweep and comparison requests remain deliberately unsupported.

docs.title: Sprint: Inverting Buck-Boost DCM channel-loss feedback
docs.text: Status: implementation complete; parent review pending.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Add scalar inverting Buck-Boost DCM loss-balanced feedback to the reusable Python/FastAPI topology workflow and Vue client. Reuse the bounded exact-curve current-ramp solver already used by Buck and Boost. Preserve positive SI magnitudes for voltage and current outputs, and identify the physical output polarity as negative.

docs.title: Model and equations
docs.text:
The inductor starts each switching period at zero current, ramps up during the switch interval, ramps down through the diode interval, then remains at zero for the idle interval. The requested output voltage is its positive magnitude; the physical Buck-Boost output is inverting, so its signed value is −Vout. With per-branch measured channel drops and equal sharing across parallel devices:

  • Switch interval: vL(I) = Vin − Vswitch(I).
  • Diode interval: vL(I) = −(Vout + Vdiode(I)).
  • dt_on = L·dI/(Vin−Vswitch(I)) and dt_diode = L·dI/(Vout+Vdiode(I)).
  • The peak current is solved from diode-interval output charge: L∫ I/(Vout+Vdiode(I)) dI = (Pout/Vout)/fsw.
  • Average input current is switch-interval charge per period; Iin = (L/T)∫ I/(Vin−Vswitch(I)) dI.
  • Average inductor current includes both ramps; average output current equals the diode-interval charge per period and the requested Pout/Vout.
  • D = ton/T, diode fraction is tdiode/T, and idle fraction is 1−D−tdiode.
  • Report the independently integrated residuals Vin·Iin−Pout−Pswitch−Pdiode and D·(Vin−Vswitch_mean) + Ddiode·(−Vout−Vdiode_mean).

All curve lookups use the existing exact temperature/gate selection and in-range current interpolation policy. The curves must include zero and cover the per-device peak; extrapolation is rejected. The requested operating point must be strictly inside the supported DCM range. A nonpositive switch-ramp voltage, missing curve coverage, failed output-charge solve, or CCM-boundary point produces an actionable error.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
1. Extend the headless scalar DCM ramp calculation to inverting Buck-Boost, with separate input/output/inductor/diode currents, switch and diode losses, RMS currents, DCM intervals, output ripple, and both residuals.
  2. Expose the result through the existing FastAPI calculation contract with SI values and output_polarity=-1; retain the existing buck-boost topology identifier and alias behavior.
  3. Update Vue labels and explanatory text so the result clearly states the inverting polarity and reports scalar DCM channel-feedback metrics. Keep loss-balanced DCM sweeps and cross-topology comparison explicitly unsupported, with actionable API errors and clear UI behavior.
  4. Add independent flat-drop and nonlinear numerical fixtures, API coverage, Vue workflow assertions, and a focused Chromium check where the repository browser environment permits.
  5. Update the migration matrix with the verified support boundary and focused evidence. Do not claim total-loss, electrothermal, sweep, or comparison parity.

docs.title: Limits and protected surfaces
docs.text:
• This is an averaged channel-conduction model. Switching, reverse recovery, gate-drive, dead-time, passive, magnetic, parasitic, and temperature-feedback losses are excluded. loss_scope remains channel_conduction_only.
  • Exact-condition switch and diode channel curves are required. No nearest condition, missing-data fallback, or extrapolation is allowed.
  • Parallel devices are identical and share current evenly.
  • Buck-Boost DCM is scalar-only. DCM loss-balanced sweeps and topology comparison remain unsupported. Explicit estimate, conduction-only, detailed, and CCM behaviors remain unchanged.
  • No TDB schema, core model, adapter, ABC, device data, Qt, ntbees2 interface, adapter, converter, evaluator, or unrelated DPT changes.

docs.title: Acceptance and validation
docs.text:
• An independently derived flat-drop case checks inverting polarity, duty, diode/idle fractions, peak, average inductor/input/output/diode currents, RMS currents, channel losses, power residual, and volt-second residual.
  • A separate nonlinear curve fixture independently integrates the ramps and verifies output charge, channel losses, residuals, and solved-trajectory output ripple. Boundary, exact curve support, no-extrapolation, and source-curve immutability cases are covered.
  • FastAPI tests verify the SI result, negative output polarity, channel-only scope, actionable missing/range/boundary errors, and DCM sweep/comparison rejection without changing CCM behavior.

docs.title: Sprint: Buck DCM channel-loss feedback
docs.text: Status: implementation complete; Sol review passed; PR pending.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Add scalar Buck DCM loss-balanced feedback using the selected switch and diode channel curves. Preserve the existing Boost DCM solve, keep comparison and sweeps CCM-only, and reject DCM feedback for Buck-Boost and Flyback.

docs.title: Model and evidence
docs.text:
In Buck DCM, inductor current begins at zero, rises during the switch interval, falls to zero during the diode interval, then remains zero for the idle interval. With output voltage reported as a positive magnitude, the inductor voltages are Vin - Vout - Vswitch(I) during the switch interval and -Vout - Vdiode(I) during the diode interval. The operation integrates each current-dependent ramp using the measured channel curve and the corresponding inductor voltage.

The output-charge condition includes both conducting intervals:

L ∫ I/(Vin−Vout−Vswitch(I)) dI + L ∫ I/(Vout+Vdiode(I)) dI = (Pout/Vout)/fsw.

The solver finds the peak current satisfying that condition. Input charge comes from the switch interval alone. It independently integrates switch and diode channel energy, then reports Vin·Iin - Pout - Pswitch - Pdiode and the time-averaged signed inductor volt-second residual. Output ripple integrates capacitor charge over the solved switch, diode, and idle trajectory.

The operation requires exact selected temperature/gate conditions, both curves to include zero current and cover the per-device peak, and no extrapolation. Parallel devices are assumed identical and share current evenly. It brackets only peaks with positive switch-ramp voltage and rejects targets at or beyond the DCM/CCM boundary.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
1. Add scalar Buck DCM feedback through the reusable Python operating-point calculation and FastAPI response. Return the solved input, output, inductor, and diode currents; separate switch and diode conduction losses; output ripple; and both balance residuals.
  2. Preserve scalar Boost DCM behavior through the shared Buck/Boost ramp integrator. Keep Buck-Boost and Flyback DCM feedback unsupported.
  3. Show the Buck DCM model and its results through the Vue workflow and include the request/result in the existing JSON export. Disable topology comparison for DCM and reject DCM sweep requests in the API.
  4. Update the migration matrix with the supported DCM boundary and validation.

docs.title: Limits and protected surfaces
docs.text:
• This is an averaged channel-conduction model. Switching, reverse-recovery, gate-drive, passive, magnetic, parasitic, and temperature-feedback losses are excluded.
  • Temperature is a one-pass estimate using the selected curve temperature; electrothermal closure is not implemented.
  • Buck and Boost DCM are scalar-only. DCM topology comparison and all DCM sweeps remain unsupported. CCM support remains unchanged.
  • Do not change the TDB schema, core models, adapters, ABCs, device records, Qt code, ntbees2 interfaces/adapters/converters/evaluator, or trial.json.

  • A separate dense nonlinear integration checks current-ramp/charge solving, both residuals, separate losses, and output ripple. A derived flat-drop CCM boundary rejects equality while accepting a nearby DCM point.
  • Python/API tests verify Buck success, unsupported Buck-Boost/Flyback DCM, DCM sweep rejection, and unchanged DCM comparison rejection.
  • Vue and Chromium checks verify the Buck DCM model label, residual display, disabled comparison, and JSON request/result export.

docs.title: Sprint: CCM channel-loss feedback vertical slice
docs.text: Status: implemented, review pending; based on the checked-in records at origin/main commit 0141c29 (PR #10 merged).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Add an explicitly bounded, reusable Python/FastAPI/UI operating mode that feeds exact-condition switch and diode channel-curve losses back into a regulated CCM operating point. The first vertical slice covers Buck, Boost, inverting Buck-Boost, and ideal-transformer Flyback when both exact-condition channel curves span the required current range. It is an averaged triangular-ripple screening model. It is not a complete topology loss model, exact nonlinear switching-period solution, or electrothermal closure.

The mode closes its included channel-loss input/output power balance by solving duty. It separately reports the averaged inductor volt-second residual. Constant-drop fixtures close both equations independently; the checked-in nonlinear gate-conditioned API fixture leaves a measured 0.0038754 V volt-second residual, so nonlinear exact closure is not claimed. No device data are altered or synthesized.

docs.title: Evidence and supported boundary
docs.text:
• TDB channel curves exist for checked-in records, and existing topology equations already define the CCM currents, ripple, polarity, and ideal Flyback turns-ratio convention.
  • The Pareto example uses a fixed 100 V to 200 V, 1 kW, 20 kHz Boost CCM boundary with checked-in CREE and Infineon devices. Its losses remain channel conduction only.
  • The inspected records do not provide positive paired switch/diode case-to-sink plus junction-to-case thermal resistances, so temperature outputs are unavailable for those candidates. Even when a temperature estimate is calculable, the selected curve temperature is fixed and the solver does not iterate the curve data against temperature.
  • At the Pareto boundary, matched switching-energy voltage conditions are absent for the compared candidates. Switching, reverse-recovery, gate-drive, passive, and magnetic losses therefore remain excluded.
  • DCM feedback is unsupported. Missing curves, mismatched conditions, and current-range extrapolation fail explicitly.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
1. Add loss-balanced to the reusable topology calculation for CCM on the four supported topologies. Solve the included channel-loss power balance, refine triangular ripple from the selected switch-channel voltage, and report both power and inductor volt-second residuals.
  2. Keep the model limits machine-readable and visible: channel-conduction-only, no switching/recovery/passive/magnetic losses, exact-condition curves only, no extrapolation, and no iterative electrothermal closure.
  3. Expose the mode through FastAPI and the existing Vue workflow, including the two balance residuals, thermal-data unavailability, unsupported DCM behavior, and topology comparison where supported.
  4. Re-run the fixed-boundary Pareto notebook with the new mode only where exact curve data support the point. Retain the explicit one-boundary, Boost-only and channel-loss-only scope in the notebook and output.

docs.title: Out of scope and protected boundary
docs.text:
